items.excerpt: ## 2. Majority quorum arithmetic and the failure envelope In a simplified majority-voting cluster of N eligible voters, a quorum is floor(N/2)+1. A **3-voter** cluster requires 2 votes, and can normally make progress with one unavailable voter if remaining voters can communicate and have necessary log state. A **5-voter** cluster requires 3. Adding an extra voting member can actually increase the quorum without increasing tolerated failures—for example 3 voters → 4 voters raises required votes from 2 to 3. items.excerpt: ## The overload boundary The overload scenario offers 30 requests per second to a 24-request-per-second pool with a 40-request queue and a one-second deadline. The run reports: - success rate 0.6488 (95% CI 0.6443-0.6534); - timeout rate 0.3495 (95% CI 0.3451-0.3540); - rejection rate 0.0005; - mean queue length 12.79; - server utilization 0.9966. The dominant failure is timeout, not rejection. The queue is large enough to absorb arrivals but not large enough to prevent deadline expiry. A report that focuses on rejection alone would miss most of the loss: rejection is 0.05% while timeout is 35.0%.
